subject: FinHealth - Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chris Miller <chris.miller@finhealth.com>, FinHealth Procurement <procurement@finhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FinHealth - Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Hi Chris — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections or anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Current in-house inference (SageMaker) is struggling with 99p latency and throughput at peak volumes; tail latency spikes during batch windows.
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI inside customer-controlled network (no model-hosted data plane).
- Procurement needs strong evidence around SOC 2, data residency, and KMS/HSM support for BYOK.

Current stack (what we heard):
- AWS (EKS + some SageMaker endpoints), VPCs per environment, existing KMS usage for at-rest keys.
- Primary traffic between your app tier and inference endpoints via private VPC connectivity.

Success criteria for PoC / evaluation:
1) Demonstrate private VPC deployment with request-forcing routing inside FinHealth VPC (no egress to public internet)
2) BYOK via AWS KMS / HSM integration (customer-managed keys)
3) 99th percentile latency < 200ms for median prompt sizes (~250 tokens) under expected concurrency
4) Visibility: audit logs for inference requests, model versioning, and token-level cost telemetry

Private/VPC / on-prem requirements we discussed:
- Support VPC peering / PrivateLink / Transit Gateway; must operate without public internet egress on inference nodes.
- BYOK via AWS KMS (bring-your-own-key) + optional HSM-backed keys for attestation.
- Option for air-gapped/on-prem bundle if required by audit, but initial preference is customer-hosted VPC with strong egress controls.
- Required artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report, network architecture diagram, and list of encryption controls.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa / Aditya to schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team (propose Wed 3/4 or Thu 3/5).
- Chris to share network diagram and primary contacts for security/compliance.
- We'll provide a short PoC plan and a draft SLA/contract addendum for dedicated/private deployment.

Attachments I've included: redwood-private-overview.pdf (high-level architecture), SOC2-SIGMA-2025.pdf (attestation).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendar invites once we confirm a time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0132

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinHealth - Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and additions from my side: 

Clarifications / added constraints:
- This is a PHI workload; HIPAA controls are required in addition to SOC 2.
- We need strict egress controls: inference nodes must not have outbound internet access. We prefer a PrivateLink or Transit Gateway model.
- BYOK is a hard requirement. We use AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed keys for our production keys.
- Data residency: production inference must remain in us-east-1.

Current infra notes:
- EKS for orchestration, Kinesis for ingestion, and Postgres RDS. We've experimented with SageMaker but are hitting cost/latency issues under load.

Success criteria (fine-tuning):
- 99p latency <= 200ms for typical prompts (250 tokens) under 100 concurrent requests.
- Detailed audit logs shipped to our SIEM (Splunk) or S3 with lifecycle.

I attached our (sanitized) network diagram: finhealth-network-diagram.pdf. Procurement will follow up on contract language and timing — they want to see a draft SOW and any compliance artifacts.

I can make Wed 3/4 10:00-11:30 PT for a technical session (Infra + Security). If that works for your team, we'll lock it in.

-Chris
